title: Small colimits and cartesian closure of the infinity category of quasicategories
statement: Fix nested universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ and use the quasicategory, coherent functor-category, mapping-space and colimit conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathrm{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$ be the infinity category of $\mathcal U$-small quasicategories, formed in a universe containing its objects. It admits all $\mathcal U$-small colimits and is cartesian closed. For $\mathcal U$-small quasicategories $A,E$, the internal Hom is the coherent functor quasicategory $\operatorname{Fun}(A,E)$, including all coherent transformations, and there are natural equivalences $$\operatorname{Fun}(T,\operatorname{Fun}(A,E))\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(T\times A,E)$$ for every $T$. The colimit and exponential constructions are natural in their diagrams and remain valid after enlarging the ambient universe to contain the target quasicategory and its coherent functor categories.

source.place: Sections 3.1.3-3.1.4, especially the internal-Hom construction preceding Proposition 3.1.3.3, Proposition 3.1.4.2 and Corollary 3.1.4.3 for cartesian closure of the quasicategory model, and Corollary 4.2.4.8 for existence of all small colimits. The universe-enlargement clause is the standard change-of-universe form of these constructions. No Mathlib declaration or Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.
